headline: High: open-webui can ingest and act on ComfyUI outputs via shared files/APIs, creating default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is file/API driven and open-webui can consume files, MCP, and tool outputs. If ComfyUI-generated images, prompts, or metadata are routed into open-webui without provenance checks, instruction-like content can be treated as trusted input. The pairwise pathway is plausible from both profiles, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into open-webui prompts or tools without sanitization
IF open-webui parses file or tool content as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of ComfyUI artifacts into chat context
Add a provenance tag to all imported files
Use a separate workspace for generated media and chat inputs
Require manual review before any tool call triggered by imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, workflows, seeds, checkpoints, and embeddings, while open-webui handles documents, files, persistent memory, and API keys. Because open-webui can access local files and mounted volumes, a shared workspace can expose sensitive model assets or user data across the pair. This is a default-capable leakage path, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted volume
IF open-webui is pointed at directories containing ComfyUI workflows, seeds, or checkpoints
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Remove shared mounts from open-webui
Restrict open-webui file access to a read-only staging folder
Store secrets outside any shared workspace
Review and prune persisted chat memory before enabling file access

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI can write model/workflow files and open-webui supports persistent shared sessions, files, and broad network/tool access. Even without explicit git or shell writes in ComfyUI, both agents can mutate overlapping local resources if deployed against the same volume or backend. Uncertainty about the exact deployment should escalate rather than downgrade.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mounted directory
IF open-webui sessions or artifacts reference files ComfyUI is updating
mitigations: Assign separate storage roots per agent
Turn off concurrent writes to shared folders
Use file locks or a queue for shared artifacts
Make one side read-only for the shared path
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can treat upstream content as chat context, tool input, or memory, and ComfyUI can generate outputs that look authoritative but are not verified facts. If open-webui forwards ComfyUI-produced text, metadata, or workflow-derived claims into downstream actions, errors can cascade into irreversible or externally visible mistakes. The interaction is plausible in default tool-enabled deployments.
conditions: IF open-webui uses ComfyUI outputs as authoritative context
IF open-webui triggers tools, messages, or memory writes from those outputs
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Mark ComfyUI outputs as untrusted by default
Disable auto-execution from imported content
Require human approval for tool calls based on generated content
Log source provenance on every forwarded artifact

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-capable and mostly local, while open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, analytics, and third-party APIs. If the pair is used on regulated or sensitive data, open-webui can move that data into external services or longer-lived storage, creating retention and residency mismatch risk. The other agent is not cited for a residency claim because its profile does not specify one.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui
IF open-webui routes that data to external APIs or persistent memory
mitigations: Disable external API connectors for sensitive projects
Shorten or clear chat retention settings
Avoid entering regulated data into open-webui
Use a local-only model backend where possible
Review export and deletion settings before use
